findings.issue_text: [Medium/bug] desktop/topic-post.scss:~291 — `.poster`/reply-to `a` color light value silently changed from lightness 30% to 70%, an unintended light-theme color regression unlike the rest of the mechanical dark-theme substitutions

[Medium/bug] mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` light branch changed from lightness 70% to 30%, unintentionally darkening hint text in light theme while all other similar changes preserve the original light value

[Medium/bug] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — user-card `h3` light branch changed from lightness 20% to 50%, lightening an intentionally darker heading, inconsistent with desktop/topic-post.scss:321 which correctly keeps 20%
[Low/bug] desktop/user.scss:522 — `.name` color light branch changed from lightness 30% to 50%, altering username visual weight; the equivalent base rule (user.scss:119) correctly keeps 30%
[Low/bug] mobile/user.scss:497 — `.name` color light branch changed from lightness 30% to 50%, same unintended light-theme value change as desktop file
[Low/test_gap] — No automated check/stylelint rule to prevent reintroduction of bare `scale-color($primary, ...)`; a lint rule or documented convention would prevent regression

goldens.comment: In .topic-meta-data h5 a, the original code had color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%) but was changed to dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%)). The lightness for the light theme changed from 30% to 70%, which is a dramatic inversion

This change for desktop/user.css changes $primary from 30% to 50% for the light theme; most other changes preserve the original $primary value and move the complement to $secondary for dark. Consider reviewing this (also applies to a similar .name change in the mobile variant).
In topic-post.css the original code used $lightness: 70% but the replacement uses $lightness: 30% for the light theme. This makes the text significantly darker than intended.

The light theme color for `.topic-meta-data h5 a` was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`, which may unintentionally reduce contrast and affect readability. This change should be reviewed to ensure it aligns with design intentions.
In mobile/user.scss line 497, the lightness value for dark themes should be inverted to 70% instead of being changed to 50%. This change may lead to unintended visual regressions in light themes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] desktop/topic-post.scss:~291 — `.poster`/reply-to `a` color light value silently changed from lightness 30% to 70%, an unintended light-theme color regression unlike the rest of the mechanical dark-theme substitutions

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` under the `.reply-to` block (~288), the `a` color changes from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. This does silently change the light-theme (primary) lightness from 30% to 70%, unlike the largely mechanical substitutions elsewhere that preserve the original primary lightness and add a corresponding secondary value. That inconsistency plausibly introduces an unintended light-theme visual regression.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] mobile/modal.scss:102 — `.custom-message-length` light branch changed from lightness 70% to 30%, unintentionally darkening hint text in light theme while all other similar changes preserve the original light value

adjudication.rationale: In app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/modal.scss, `.custom-message-length` was changed from `color: scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%);` to `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%));`, which alters the light-theme (first arg) lightness from 70% to 30%. Elsewhere in this diff, the light-theme argument typically preserves the original `$primary` lightness value, so this stands out as an inconsistent and likely unintended darkening in the light theme.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — user-card `h3` light branch changed from lightness 20% to 50%, lightening an intentionally darker heading, inconsistent with desktop/topic-post.scss:321 which correctly keeps 20%

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss`, within the `a.star h3` rule, the color was changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, which does lighten the light-theme branch from 20% to 50%. In contrast, `app/assets/stylesheets/desktop/topic-post.scss` keeps the light-theme branch at 20% (`dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), ...)`). This is a verifiable inconsistency introduced by the diff and likely a visual regression on mobile.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/bug] mobile/user.scss:497 — `.name` color light branch changed from lightness 30% to 50%, same unintended light-theme value change as desktop file

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `mobile/user.scss` `.name` changing from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), ...)`, which indeed alters the light-theme (first argument) lightness from 30% to 50%. The same pattern appears in `desktop/user.scss` for `.name`. However, the claim that this is an "unintended" bug/regression isn’t provable from the diff alone—this could be an intentional visual adjustment while adding `dark-light-choose`—so it’s best treated as a concrete review concern to confirm intent rather than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] — No automated check/stylelint rule to prevent reintroduction of bare `scale-color($primary, ...)`; a lint rule or documented convention would prevent regression

adjudication.rationale: The diff only shows many CSS changes replacing `scale-color($primary, ...)` with `dark-light-choose(...)`. It does not include any stylelint configuration, CI checks, or documentation changes, so the claim that there is “no automated check/stylelint rule” to prevent reintroducing bare `scale-color($primary, ...)` cannot be verified from this diff alone.
